summary: Defines data backup frequency, storage requirements, testing procedures, and recovery time objectives.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Data backup schedule with frequency, scope, and storage location documentation
Backup test results with recovery time objective (RTO) validation records
Off-site or cloud backup storage verification documentation
Backup restoration test logs with completion timestamps
justification: Corridor row 2-053 'Contingency Plan' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Contingency Plan standard (45 CFR §164.308(a)(7)), which explicitly requires a Data Backup Plan as one of its five required implementation specifications. IT-DR-001 governs data backup frequency, storage, testing, and RTO — the operational implementation of the HIPAA Contingency Plan's data backup component. Evidence: P, D. Note: DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_FAMILY with IT-DR-002 — both map to 2-053 as complementary Contingency Plan sub-components (backup vs. disaster recovery).

summary: Establishes the IT disaster recovery plan including recovery procedures, testing frequency, and communication protocols.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Written IT Disaster Recovery Plan with recovery procedures and RTO/RPO targets
Annual DR test results with communication protocol documentation
Emergency mode operations plan
IT continuity activation decision tree and notification records
justification: Corridor row 2-053 'Contingency Plan' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Contingency Plan standard, which explicitly requires a Disaster Recovery Plan as one of its five required implementation specifications. IT-DR-002 governs the IT disaster recovery plan including recovery procedures, testing, and communication — the disaster recovery component of the HIPAA contingency plan. Evidence: P, D. Note: DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_FAMILY with IT-DR-001 — both map to 2-053 representing complementary required sub-components. ACHC surveyors evaluate these collectively under 2-053; framework governance should establish parent relationship to the HIPAA Contingency Plan to prevent workflow double-counting.

summary: Mandates system audit logging standards including retention periods, review frequency, and alert thresholds.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Audit log configuration documentation for all systems containing PHI

justification: Corridor row 2-059 'HIPAA Security Audit Controls' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Audit Controls standard (45 CFR §164.312(b)), which requires hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms to record and examine activity in information systems containing PHI. IT-DR-003 governs audit logging standards, retention, review frequency, and alert thresholds — the operational implementation of this Corridor row. Evidence: P, D.

summary: Establishes security and compliance requirements for cloud-based services and off-premises data storage.
corridorPolicyTitle: Contingency Plan; Device and Media Controls
realEvidenceArtifacts: Cloud service inventory with security classification and BAA documentation
Cloud service security assessment reports (SOC 2, HITRUST, or equivalent)
Off-premises data storage agreements with security requirements
Cloud data residency and sovereignty compliance documentation
justification: Corridor row 2-053 'Contingency Plan' covers off-premises data storage as a contingency element, and row 2-057 'Device and Media Controls' (HH5-1B) covers media management including electronic media used for data storage. IT-DR-004 governs cloud-specific security requirements — cloud service security assessments, cloud BAAs, SaaS governance, and data sovereignty controls. Cloud computing as a service category post-dates the Corridor's media controls framework. PARTIAL because the physical media and contingency rows structurally cover data storage governance, but cloud-specific compliance requirements (CSP security posture, shared responsibility models, data residency) substantially exceed these rows' scope.

summary: Defines the process for detecting, reporting, investigating, and responding to information security incidents.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Security incident response plan with detection, triage, and response procedures
Security incident log with detection timestamps and response timelines
Post-incident analysis reports
Incident notification records to HIPAA Breach Notification requirements (if applicable)
justification: Corridor row 2-052 'Security Incident Procedures' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Security Incident Procedures standard (45 CFR §164.308(a)(6)), which requires policies and procedures to address security incidents including their identification, response, and documentation. IT-DR-005 governs the full security incident response lifecycle — detection, reporting, investigation, and response — an exact match to the Corridor row. Evidence: P, D.

summary: Defines EHR system administration standards including configuration management, update procedures, and data integrity controls.
corridorPolicyTitle: Interface of Patient Data and Management Systems; Integrity Controls
realEvidenceArtifacts: EHR system configuration baseline documentation
System update and patch approval workflow records
Data integrity audit records demonstrating record accuracy and completeness
EHR change log with version control documentation
justification: Corridor row 2-010 'Interface of Patient Data and Management Systems' (HH2-5A) covers the interface between patient data and management information systems — the structural role that EHR systems occupy. Row 2-060 'Integrity Controls' (HH5-1B) covers HIPAA data integrity requirements for electronic PHI systems. IT-SA-001 governs EHR system administration — configuration management, update procedures, and data integrity controls — as an IT operational function. PARTIAL because the information system interface and integrity rows establish the regulatory context, but EHR configuration management, change approval workflows, and rollback procedures are IT administrative governance beyond Corridor scope.

summary: Establishes standards for software procurement, licensing compliance, and shadow IT prevention.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs software procurement, licensing compliance, or shadow IT prevention. Software asset management and procurement governance are IT operational disciplines with no ACHC/CoP crosswalk equivalent. These functions belong to the Modern Operational Governance Layer.

summary: Defines change management procedures for IT systems including testing, approval, and rollback requirements.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs IT system change management procedures. While the HIPAA Security Rule Evaluation standard (2-054, HH5-1B) requires periodic technical and non-technical evaluation of security controls, IT change management as a discipline — change advisory boards, change request approvals, testing gates, and rollback procedures — is an ITIL/IT governance function that exceeds the Corridor's security evaluation row. Forcing this to 2-054 would collapse change management governance into security evaluation — a categorical error. Modern Operational Governance Layer.

summary: Establishes security assessment requirements for technology vendors and third parties with access to agency systems or data.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Vendor security assessment questionnaires and completed evaluation records
Technology vendor BAA inventory with execution dates
Third-party security review reports (SOC 2, penetration test summaries)
Vendor risk register with security rating by vendor category
justification: Corridor row 2-033 'Business Associates' (HH2-5C.01) governs PHI contractual controls for vendors — the contractual/agreement layer of vendor management. IT-SA-004 establishes active security assessment requirements for technology vendors — evaluating vendor security posture through questionnaires, SOC 2 reviews, and penetration test results, and maintaining a vendor risk register. The Corridor row requires that BAs execute agreements; IT-SA-004 requires that vendors are also actively assessed for security fitness. PARTIAL because the BA agreement row is the closest structural parent, but the security assessment program is a proactive risk management overlay beyond the Corridor's contractual compliance requirement.

summary: Defines physical security requirements for servers, workstations, and devices containing PHI.
corridorPolicyTitle: Facility Access Controls; Workstation Use and Security
realEvidenceArtifacts: Server room/data closet physical access control documentation (badge access logs, lock records)
Workstation physical security compliance checklist
Device inventory with physical security classification
Physical access control review records for IT assets
justification: Corridor row 2-055 'Facility Access Controls' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Physical Safeguards — Facility Access Controls standard (45 CFR §164.310(a)), requiring policies to limit physical access to electronic information systems. Row 2-056 'Workstation Use and Security' (HH5-1B) implements the Workstation Security standard (45 CFR §164.310(c)), requiring physical safeguards for workstations accessing PHI. IT-SA-005 governs physical security of servers, workstations, and devices — the operational implementation of both rows. Evidence: P, D.

summary: Establishes the agency's comprehensive information security program including governance, risk management, and security controls.
corridorPolicyTitle: Security Management Process; Security of PHI
realEvidenceArtifacts: Information security program charter with governance structure
Annual security risk assessment report
Security control inventory and status documentation
Security program annual review and board/leadership presentation
justification: Corridor row 2-048 'Security Management Process' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Administrative Safeguards — Security Management Process standard (45 CFR §164.308(a)(1)), requiring risk analysis, risk management, sanction policy, and information system activity review. Row 2-045 'Security of PHI' provides the overarching PHI security governance requirement. IT-SC-001 establishes a comprehensive information security program that encompasses HIPAA compliance (covered by 2-048) plus enterprise security governance extending to non-PHI systems, network security, third-party risk, and security engineering functions not captured in the HIPAA administrative safeguards framework. PARTIAL because 2-048 is the correct structural parent, but an enterprise information security program exceeds HIPAA's PHI-specific scope.

summary: Defines access control standards including role-based access, password requirements, and multi-factor authentication.
corridorPolicyTitle: Access Controls: Technical Safeguards; Information Access Management; Person or Entity Authentication
realEvidenceArtifacts: Role-based access control configuration documentation by user role
User access review records (periodic access certification)
Password policy documentation with complexity and rotation requirements
MFA enrollment records for applicable systems and user categories
justification: Corridor rows 2-058 'Access Controls: Technical Safeguards' (implementing 45 CFR §164.312(a)), 2-050 'Information Access Management' (implementing 45 CFR §164.308(a)(4)), and 2-061 'Person or Entity Authentication' (implementing 45 CFR §164.312(d)) collectively and directly govern access control and user authentication requirements. IT-SC-002's content — role-based access, password requirements, and MFA — are the operational implementations of these three HIPAA Technical Safeguards rows. The addition of MFA (a modern security enhancement beyond the original HIPAA rule's required specifications) is an operational security layer that strengthens rather than contradicts the Corridor's authentication requirement. Evidence: P, D.

summary: Mandates encryption standards for PHI at rest and in transit per HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Encryption standard specification document (AES-256 or equivalent)
TLS configuration documentation for all PHI transmission channels
Encrypted device inventory with encryption method verification
Encryption key management policy and key rotation records
justification: Corridor row 2-062 'Transmission Security' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Transmission Security standard (45 CFR §164.312(e)), requiring encryption or equivalent measures for PHI in transit. Row 2-060 'Integrity Controls' (implementing 45 CFR §164.312(c)) governs mechanisms to authenticate electronic PHI integrity — which in practice requires encryption at rest. IT-SC-003 mandates encryption for PHI at rest and in transit per HIPAA — the operational implementation of these two rows. Evidence: P, D.

summary: Establishes network security controls including firewall configuration, intrusion detection, and network segmentation.
corridorPolicyTitle: Security Management Process; Access Controls: Technical Safeguards
realEvidenceArtifacts: Firewall configuration standards and change management records
Network architecture diagram showing segmentation and PHI zones
Intrusion detection/prevention system (IDS/IPS) configuration and alert records
Annual network security assessment or penetration test results
justification: Corridor row 2-048 'Security Management Process' requires risk analysis and management (which implies network security controls as risk mitigations), and row 2-058 'Access Controls: Technical Safeguards' covers technical access controls that include network access management. IT-SC-004 governs firewall configuration, intrusion detection, and network segmentation — specific cybersecurity engineering disciplines that the HIPAA Security Rule rows imply as controls but do not specifically govern. PARTIAL because the security management and access control rows are the structural parents, but network security engineering (firewall rulesets, IDS/IPS tuning, DMZ architecture, VLAN segmentation) is a modern cybersecurity operational layer beyond the Corridor's HIPAA-level controls framework.

summary: Establishes standards for endpoint protection including antivirus, anti-malware, and patch management requirements.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Endpoint security software deployment inventory (antivirus/anti-malware coverage)
Patch management schedule with critical patch deployment SLA documentation
Endpoint security scan results and remediation records
Mobile device management (MDM) enrollment and compliance status reports
justification: Corridor row 2-056 'Workstation Use and Security' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Workstation Security standard (45 CFR §164.310(c)), requiring physical and logical safeguards for workstations. IT-SC-005 governs endpoint protection — antivirus/anti-malware deployment, patch management, and EDR (endpoint detection and response). These are specific technical implementations of workstation security that exceed the Corridor row's scope: the Corridor requires workstation security measures exist; IT-SC-005 defines the specific technical controls (antivirus signatures, patch windows, malware response procedures) that constitute modern endpoint protection. PARTIAL because 2-056 is the correct structural parent, but the technical endpoint protection program substantially exceeds the workstation security row's general requirement.

summary: Establishes data classification levels and corresponding handling, storage, transmission, and destruction requirements.
corridorPolicyTitle: Security of PHI; Device and Media Controls
realEvidenceArtifacts: Data classification taxonomy documentation (classification levels and criteria)
Data handling procedures by classification level
Media disposal and destruction records with method and date
Data classification compliance audit records
justification: Corridor row 2-045 'Security of PHI' governs the security of protected health information — the most sensitive classification tier. Row 2-057 'Device and Media Controls' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Physical Safeguards — Device and Media Controls standard (45 CFR §164.310(d)), covering media handling and disposal. IT-SC-006 establishes a multi-tier data classification system extending beyond HIPAA's binary PHI/non-PHI framework to govern data handling across public, internal, confidential, and restricted tiers. PARTIAL because the PHI security and media controls rows cover the most restricted tier exactly, but the full classification taxonomy — including data lifecycle governance, retention matrices, and multi-tier handling procedures — is an information governance framework that exceeds the Corridor's PHI-specific rows.

summary: Defines security requirements for mobile devices, personal devices, and remote access to agency systems.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollment records for agency and personal devices
BYOD security agreement and enrollment documentation
Remote wipe capability verification and test records
Mobile device acceptable use acknowledgment records
justification: Corridor row 2-057 'Device and Media Controls' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Physical Safeguards — Device and Media Controls standard, covering hardware and electronic media containing PHI. IT-UP-001 governs mobile device and BYOD security — including MDM enrollment, personal device enrollment, remote wipe, and conditional access policies. The Corridor row covers devices generally; BYOD as a formal program (personal device enrollment, MDM policy enforcement, containerization of PHI on personal devices) is a modern enterprise mobility management concept that substantially exceeds the Corridor's device controls row. PARTIAL because 2-057 is the structural parent, but the BYOD program infrastructure is a modern operational overlay.

summary: Establishes acceptable use standards for agency internet, email, and communication systems.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) with workforce acknowledgment signatures
Internet use monitoring policy disclosure to workforce
Email security policy with attachment and link handling requirements
AUP training completion records
justification: Corridor row 2-056 'Workstation Use and Security' (HH5-1B) is the closest structural parent — workstation use policies implicitly govern how agency systems (including internet and email) are used. IT-UP-002 establishes a formal Acceptable Use Policy governing prohibited internet activities, email security behaviors, and monitoring rights. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence because 2-056 establishes that workstation use must be governed, but the AUP's content — specific internet restrictions, email phishing protocols, monitoring disclosure, and enforcement mechanisms — are IT operational governance beyond the workstation security row's HIPAA-security focus.

summary: Defines standards for agency and employee social media use to protect patient privacy and agency reputation.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Social media policy with workforce acknowledgment records
Social media prohibited conduct guidelines
PHI disclosure incident reports tied to social media (if applicable)
Social media monitoring and response protocol documentation
justification: Corridor row 2-044 'Social Media' appears in Section 2 of the crosswalk but has no ACHC standard, CoP, or Title 22 citation — it is an acknowledged policy area without crosswalk targets. IT-UP-003 governs the same subject — social media use by the agency and workforce. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence: the Corridor acknowledges social media as a required policy area (hence its appearance in the crosswalk) but provides no regulatory anchor. The absence of ACHC standards from 2-044 means this mapping has structural acknowledgment but no surveyable standard. Unusual in the Corridor crosswalk — one of the few rows with no regulatory citation.

justification: Corridor row 2-051 'Security Awareness and Training' (HH5-1B) implements the HIPAA Security Rule Administrative Safeguards — Security Awareness and Training standard (45 CFR §164.308(a)(5)), requiring security awareness training for all workforce members. IT-UP-004 mandates initial and ongoing security awareness training with documented completion — an exact match to the Corridor row. Evidence: P, D.
